title: Rigveda 7.88: To Varuna
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 7.88: To Varuna: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 7.88 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Varuna. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 7, the family book of Vasiṣṭha. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 547v-548r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 7.88.1-3 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 6, varga 10); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 547v
translation.original_text:
1pra śu̱ndhyuva̱ṁ varu̍ṇāya̱ preṣṭhā̍m ma̱tiṁ va̍siṣṭha mī̱ḻhuṣe̍ bharasva | ya ī̍m a̱rvāñca̱ṁ kara̍te̱ yaja̍traṁ sa̱hasrā̍magha̱ṁ vṛṣa̍ṇam bṛ̱hanta̍m ||
2adhā̱ nv a̍sya sa̱ṁdṛśa̍ṁ jaga̱nvān a̱gner anī̍ka̱ṁ varu̍ṇasya maṁsi | sva1̱̍r yad aśma̍nn adhi̱pā u̱ andho̱ 'bhi mā̱ vapu̍r dṛ̱śaye̍ ninīyāt ||
3ā yad ru̱hāva̱ varu̍ṇaś ca̱ nāva̱m pra yat sa̍mu̱dram ī̱rayā̍va̱ madhya̍m | adhi̱ yad a̱pāṁ snubhi̱ś carā̍va̱ pra pre̱ṅkha ī̍ṅkhayāvahai śu̱bhe kam ||
translation.text:
1PRESENT to Varuṇa thine hymn, Vasishṭha, bright, most delightful to the Bounteous Giver, Who bringeth on to us the Bull, the lofty, the Holy, laden with a thousand treasures.
2And now, as I am come before his presence, I take the face of Varuṇa for Agni's. So might he bring-Lord also of the darkness-the light in heaven that I may see its beauty!
3When Varuṇa and I embark together and urge our boat into the midst of ocean, We, when we ride o'er ridges of the waters, will swing within that swing and there be happy.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 547v (numbered 68v by the scribe) (OPenn image 548, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.87.5 ‹-etam divi pra-īṅkham hiraṇyayam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 548r (numbered 69r by the scribe), begins in RV 7.88.4 ‹stotāram vipraḥ sudina-tve ahvām›. Verses 7.88.1-3 end on this page.

2adha | nu | asya | sam-dṛśam | jaganvān | agneḥ | anīkam | varuṇasya | maṃs i | svaḥ | yat | aśman | adhi-pāḥ | oṃ iti | andhaḥ | abhi | mā | vapuḥ | dṛśaye | ninīyāt

translation.original_ref: RV 7.88.4-7 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 6, varga 10); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 548r
translation.original_text:
4vasi̍ṣṭhaṁ ha̱ varu̍ṇo nā̱vy ādhā̱d ṛṣi̍ṁ cakāra̱ svapā̱ maho̍bhiḥ | sto̱tāra̱ṁ vipra̍ḥ sudina̱tve ahnā̱ṁ yān nu dyāva̍s ta̱tana̱n yād u̱ṣāsa̍ḥ ||
5kva1̱̍ tyāni̍ nau sa̱khyā ba̍bhūvu̱ḥ sacā̍vahe̱ yad a̍vṛ̱kam pu̱rā ci̍t | bṛ̱hanta̱m māna̍ṁ varuṇa svadhāvaḥ sa̱hasra̍dvāraṁ jagamā gṛ̱haṁ te̍ ||
6ya ā̱pir nityo̍ varuṇa pri̱yaḥ san tvām āgā̍ṁsi kṛ̱ṇava̱t sakhā̍ te | mā ta̱ ena̍svanto yakṣin bhujema ya̱ndhi ṣmā̱ vipra̍ḥ stuva̱te varū̍tham ||
7dhru̱vāsu̍ tvā̱su kṣi̱tiṣu̍ kṣi̱yanto̱ vy a1̱̍smat pāśa̱ṁ varu̍ṇo mumocat | avo̍ vanvā̱nā adi̍ter u̱pasthā̍d yū̱yam pā̍ta sva̱stibhi̱ḥ sadā̍ naḥ ||
translation.text:
4Varuṇa placed Vasishṭha in the vessel, and deftly with his might made him a R̥ishi. When days shone bright the Sage made him a singer, while the heavens broadened and the Dawns were lengthened.
5What hath become of those our ancient friendships, when without enmity we walked together? I, Varuṇa, thou glorious Lord, have entered thy lofty home, thine house with thousand portals.
6If he, thy true ally, hath sinned against thee, still, Varuṇa, he is the friend thou lovedst. Let us not, Living One, as sinners I know thee: give shelter, as a Sage, to him who lauds thee.
7While we abide in these fixed habitations, and from the lap of Aditi win favour, May Varuṇa untie the bond that binds us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 548r (numbered 69r by the scribe) (OPenn image 548, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.88.4 ‹stotāram vipraḥ sudina-tve ahvām›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 548v (numbered 69v by the scribe), begins in RV 7.89.5 ‹-dharma yuyopima mā naḥ›. Verses 7.88.4-7 end on this page; 7.88.4 begins on fol. 547v (numbered 68v by the scribe).
